provenance.source: Original RGB source, inspected at native resolution.

decision_contract.authored_base_wash: The visible sand and watercolor wash at the base is foreground and must be retained.
decision_contract.uniform_paper: Uniform cream paper beyond the visibly authored fade is background and must be transparent.
decision_contract.terminal_fade: The exact terminal transition from authored wash to cream paper is not machine-labelled and remains mandatory human review.

annotation_quality_audit.rule: At least 75 percent of each intended boundary must genuinely be pigment-colored at RGB distance 80 or more from paper; intentional white or cream subject highlights are foreground and cannot be treated as contamination.
annotation_quality_audit.correction: Replaced edge-left-pale-bubbles with edge-left-salmon-coral-outer. The bubble crop contains intentional white and cream highlights and therefore could not satisfy the rule independently of a candidate. The replacement has a continuous salmon-pigment silhouette; its white highlights are internal, not boundary truth.
annotation_quality_audit.enclosed_background_result: PASS: all five centers are visibly blank cream paper, not pale paint; their source RGB distance from white is at most 17.4, consistent with this source's cream paper.

paper_contract_audit.decision: Materially cream rather than white; freeze a case-level paper_rgb for reconstruction and edge-distance checks.

provenance.note: All guards and edge boxes were selected from the original source before any candidate was inspected. Sure-FG points avoid the unresolved terminal fade while explicitly protecting pale bubbles, kelp, shells, coral, and interior base wash. Sure-BG points lie in visually blank exterior or interior paper.

sure_foreground.why: Pale blue paint on the upper bubble is authored illustration.
Very pale blue bubble body must not be mistaken for cream paper.
Small translucent bubble at upper left is foreground.
Pale yellow kelp tip is painted art.
Thin pale green kelp blade must remain.
Cream seahorse belly is foreground despite its paper-like value.
Pale peach fish body is illustration.
Light pink coral tip in sparse central paper must remain.
Pale blue fan behind the orange coral is foreground.
Pale upper coral tip is painted art.
Cream shell surface at the base is foreground.
Pale orange starfish arm is illustration.
Left authored base wash is foreground, not cream paper.
Central pale sand wash lies safely inside the authored base.
Right pale sand wash lies inside the visibly authored base.

sure_background_enclosed.why: Blank cream paper between the left coral trunk and branch.
Second blank paper pocket between left coral branches.
Blank paper pocket among upper right pink branches.
Blank paper in the narrow central kelp gap.
Blank paper enclosed by a lower right coral fork.

edge_probes.why: The left salmon coral has a visibly pigment-lined outer silhouette; intentional cream highlights lie inside the subject and are not boundary truth.
edge_probes.source_semantic_audit: PASS: visibly more than three quarters of the intended outer contour is salmon or pink pigment at the frozen paper-distance premise.

edge_probes.why: Thin yellow-green ribbons require colored, not paper-white, boundary pixels.
edge_probes.source_semantic_audit: PASS: the intended outer ribbon contours are continuously outlined in yellow-green pigment; white strokes are internal highlights.

edge_probes.why: Pale pink upper coral tips are a high-risk fringe region.
edge_probes.source_semantic_audit: PASS: the intended coral silhouette is bounded by pink or salmon pigment around well over three quarters of its perimeter; white dots and streaks are internal highlights.

human_review.why: Pixel metrics cannot decide whether every translucent watercolor edge looks natural.
The exact terminal transition from authored sand wash to uniform cream paper is intentionally not machine-labelled.
Extremely pale bubbles and splash marks need direct visual confirmation.
Dense coral forks combine pale paint with several true paper pockets.
